rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Over-hedge detector.

Applying the senior-engineer test: this states a decision CRITERION (when to legitimately stop a walk-away run), not a reassurance-for-anxiety sentence appended to a division-of-labour line -- it doesn't apologise for a choice already made, it defines when a choice is correct. rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Value-prop / positioning framing belongs in sales copy + project strategy docs, NOT student-facing curriculum body.

'Goal drift' / 'Context rot' / 'Plausible-but-wrong' are this module's own pre-read-established vocabulary (backing block: 'the pre-read carries the colour'), earned within the same module immediately upstream (reading-the-return.md), not planted ahead of arc.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No combative verbs about the agent in body prose.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Headers must be literally true about the mechanism.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Machine-cadence fat — the shape of good prose without the content.
rules_evaluated.evidence: (a) Empty negation: L27 'You're diagnosing, not fixing' and L29 'You are not holding the codebase' both negate a real reader instinct (jump to fixing; think you must read the codebase yourself), not a strawman -- kept. L87 'Not the plan-mode plan' is load-bearing disambiguation against a real Claude Code primitive collision (check_student_facing rule 20), not empty. rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't state a count the adjacent list already holds.

The Phase-3 verifier-shape menu (three bulleted options) has no adjacent numeral in its lead-in (L63 'Pick the verifier shape that matches the failure that cost you most' -- no count stated). No violation found.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Say it once, at its most concrete, then at most one sentence that generalises it. Style, not a gate.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L109 is the exemplar of the GOOD shape the rule describes: 'Now the re-send. Same task, packaged this time, and notice the prompt: it shrank while the task stayed the same.' (concrete instance) + 'The packaging does the explaining; the prompt invokes it.' (the one sentence that makes it portable) -- then stops. No abstract-twin, no widening qualifier ('or rule', 'or context-dependent') found anywhere in body. The L133 RLHF passage is a multi-sentence paragraph but each sentence adds new content (closes -> expect X -> why -> stakes -> concrete rescue -> decision), not a restatement of one idea at two altitudes.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Aspirational destination, never corrective gap.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No corrective-gap or ability-tier phrasing found ('you already think you're using X', 'at your scale', 'for a beginner', 'a senior would already know') -- zero hits. No tourist/practitioner-style identity-criterion contrast is drawn in this file. The pre-prompt gate at L13 ('**HOX** You should be in the worktree now. Make sure you are not continuing in the original repo or on its branch.') is plausibly-failable at this exact point (M4's send-off ran in the original repo; this is the first M5 beat after the fork) -- this is in fact the compendium's OWN cited exemplar of a real gate ('a **HOX** guarding the wrong worktree fails visibly, within a minute, unmissably', check_student_facing rule 9).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Earn every technical term on first use.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 'worktree' is earned in the immediately-preceding same-module exercise (fork-the-worktree.md), not cold here. rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Memory vs context — use deliberately.

'the context window fills' (L87, of plan.md) correctly uses 'context' for ambient runtime state; the CLAUDE.md/CLAUDE.local.md/observations/ references (L113, L140) are correctly treated as persistent artefacts without being mislabeled 'memory'; plan.md is precisely called 'the agent's working document', never 'memory'.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Golden path only in body — THIS RULE HAS AN EXCEPTION; read to the boundary before cutting anything.

Both are the rule's own licensed shape (time-critical / non-obvious rescues that qualify for body), not routed-away FAQ branches.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Trust Claude's defaults for structure.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Two places specify output shape, both teaching-moment-justified per the rule's own exception: the Phase-3 verifier-branch spec (shell-hook/judge/Ralph re-feed each get a distinct ask) directly serves the lesson of differentiating verifier shapes; the final send-off's 'Report back as three lists, no narrative, no hedging' directly counters the RLHF-polish risk the body names two sentences later. rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't smuggle another module's voice.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Trust the prompt over the scaffold.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Exercise headers pass the build-squint test.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No placeholders inside fences.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Scanned all 10 fences for bracket placeholders ([BRACKETS], [path from step 1]) -- zero found. The Phase-3 fence's dangling 'Shape:' line is the licensed open-hook pattern (rule 1d: internal paragraph then single open-hook colon line, all in one fence), matched exactly by the body's own lead-in 'Drop the shape name after the colon, one of: judge, shell-hook, Ralph re-feed.'

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every prompt block: one-sentence action lead-in.

Two instances directly match the compendium's own newly-added prescriptive sub-cases: the Phase-3 prompt's lead-in is exactly the rule's 'dangling-colon' sub-case exemplar ('Drop the shape name after the colon...' with no redundant summary); the smoke-test prompt has no separate lead-in sentence because its `## Prove the verifier actually fires` header already carries the command verb (rule 2c). rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Canonical shape — lead-in, label with destination, blank line, fence.

No 'copy →' prefix, no '(end of prompt)' closer, no blockquote/backtick wrapping found. The two bare `/rename` fences carry no Prompt label, consistent with this training's established convention that session-naming utility commands are exempt housekeeping, not task prompts (the `/clear` fence, by contrast, gets the full label since it is a real alternative the student chooses).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Chain by back-reference + deterministic path, never invented alias.

No invented filename alias found.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Chained-prompt isolation — don't leak downstream pipeline.

The rule's stated harm is collapsing a designed CONTRAST between an unwarned and a warned pass (its examples: pre-grilling, deferring hard choices because 'grill will catch it'); Phase 1 -> Phase 3 in this exercise is not built as a contrast pair the way a plan/grill exercise is, so there is no contrast to collapse. The sentence instead gives Claude the stakes needed to rank failures by real cost rather than as an arbitrary label. Harm not present; stays inside the rule.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No session-resets mid-phase.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The file's only `/clear` offer (L123) sits exactly at the designed Phase-5 session boundary (a fresh M5-long-run session vs. staying in the exercise session), not mid-phase; every other phase runs warm in the same continuous session.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Markdown shout (`**bold**`, `*italic*`) inside fenced prompts = dead weight in Claude Code.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Minimal hand-off + Claude self-augments for send-off prompts.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Grill before save — collaborative quality at artefact assembly.

For each, recommend an answer.' -- the required grill-before-persistence pattern for an artefact (reference + plan.md) that downstream work depends on.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Tell me what you wrote, not show me what you'll write.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The final send-off (a side-effect-heavy, long-running action) correctly uses post-action report ('Report back as three lists...'), the rule's default. The two show-before-save instances (Phase 3 verifier, Phase 4 reference/plan.md) are governed by the more specific artefact-assembly grill-before-save rules (20/35), which explicitly name 'verifier script' and 'reference doc'/'plan.md' as the licensed pre-confirm category -- not a violation of this rule's general default.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't restate session CWD inside prompt body.

The one absolute-looking path (`~/.claude/projects/`, for the session transcript) points to a different filesystem location entirely (Claude Code's own transcript store), not a restatement of the worktree's own CWD -- not this rule's concern.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Name consumer at write time — `Save it as <path>` requires downstream reader.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strong-bold prompt label is exactly `**Prompt**` — custom labels break renderer.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Git-output greps asserting exact-N need multi-result fallback.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The one candidate ('commits since the \'M4 starting point\' commit', Phase-1-P2 fence) references a commit the worktree itself was forked from (per fork-the-worktree.md), identifiable via git ancestry (merge-base) rather than a fragile commit-message text grep -- not the fuzzy exact-N grep shape this rule targets. `git branch --show-current` in the final prompt is deterministically single-valued by definition, also out of scope.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Disambiguation, anchors, and decision logic that bind Claude live INSIDE prompt fence.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Read every fence in isolation from body. The highest-risk case, the cold final send-off prompt, is fully self-contained: deterministic anchors only (`git branch --show-current`, `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` env var, `./task.md` relative path, explicit 'find them by listing the worktree' discovery instruction) -- executes correctly with zero reliance on body callouts.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Repeated Q&A → premature re-edits. Separate iteration from persistence.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The Phase-4 grill matches all five required elements: (a) explicit operator trigger ('Don't touch either file until I say \'lock it in.\''), (b) sectional edits ('use Edit on the changed section, not Write on the whole file'), (c) batch cadence ('Ask three questions at a time'), (d) slowness-watch callout ('> **Timebox check.** Two or three rounds fit the slot...'), (e) explicit Approve section ('## Approve / Say *lock it in.* The agent writes both files.').

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Wide prompts split by logical move — paragraph breaks = cheapest scan-affordance.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Every fence is well-segmented by move (Phase-3's conditional branches each get their own paragraph, exactly matching the rule's own conditional-split example). Closest-to-violating: the final prompt's 'Rules:' line joins four short clauses by semicolon (cadence / don't paper over failures / stuck-fallback / walking-away framing) in one paragraph -- but rule 19 explicitly specifies a compact, semicolon-joined 'Rules (minimal...)' block as the intended shape for this exact send-off section, and the four clauses are short, parallel and topically unified (operating constraints for an unattended run), so splitting would fight the minimal-handoff design rather than aid scanning. Stays inside the rule by the more specific rule 19's own design intent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body lead-in mirrors prompt's opening phrasing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked every lead-in/fence pair. Strongest evidence is the diff'd fix itself: the send-off lead-in now reads 'Ask Claude to record this session's run coordinates, then re-run the same task...' which mirrors the prompt's actual opening move ('write a protected block... headed `Run coordinates (do not rewrite or remove)`...') -- the noun phrase 'run coordinates' now appears in both, resolving what was previously a mismatch (old lead-in only said 're-run the same task', omitting the prompt's actual first move). The Phase-2 lead-in ('walk each diagnosed failure backwards into the validation that would have caught it') mirrors its prompt's opening ('walk it backwards: what specific validation would have caught it') almost verbatim.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Verify session boundary before deciding prompt's context-carrying.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Verified session boundary by reading module flow, not the frontmatter context line. Phases 1-4 run warm in one continuous session (no `/clear` until the designed Phase-5 boundary); every warm back-reference (\'the three failures we just named\', \'the verifier you just built\', \'the task we ran un-packaged\') is genuinely produced in-session by an earlier prompt in this same file (e.g. \'un-packaged\' is itself first spoken inside the Phase-1-P2 fence, satisfying 40b's warm-does-not-mean-referent-present test). The final send-off correctly treats its session as cold and is fully self-contained (see rule 34). No concurrent-worktree corollary (40a) applies -- this exercise runs one worktree, sequentially.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Artifact-vs-STOP tail ordering — last imperative wins.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The final send-off's tail places 'I'm walking away' inside the Rules block (framing, not a stop-trigger blocking the task) and puts the load-bearing 'Report back as three lists...' spec at the very end of the whole prompt -- the last, most recent directive is the artefact/report Claude should in fact produce last, matching the rule's own prescribed fix pattern exactly. The earlier conditional 'if you can't determine the path, stop and tell me rather than guessing' is scoped narrowly to one sub-step and does not block the main task write.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Output shape — trust Claude's defaults, don't pad.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The two places that specify output shape (Phase-3's judge/shell-hook/Ralph branches; the send-off's three-list report format) are both teaching-moment-dependent per the rule's own allowance (differentiating verifier types is the lesson; the report format directly counters the RLHF-polish risk named two sentences later, functioning like the rule's own 'scoring format for an eval judge' example). No unjustified trailing shape spec found elsewhere.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A take-home prompt asks for one bounded build.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The final unattended send-off asks for exactly ONE build: re-run the single task already defined in `task.md` since M4, using the packaging just built. Singular, deterministic starting point (task.md), clear check (the verifier) -- no plural deliverable, no 'per X' clause, no unresolved 'worth...' qualifier; contrasts favourably with the rule's own cited bad example.
